_meta.purpose: Calibrated decision parameters for the L1 unified scorecard. Two independent machineries live here: (1) RULE-BASED HARD VETOES grounded in regulatory genotoxicity/cardiac-safety guidance (ICH M7, S7B, S2(R1)) and deterministic structural chemistry, and (2) a MULTI-PARAMETER-OPTIMIZATION (MPO) DESIRABILITY composite that ranks a candidate the way a medicinal-chemistry portfolio committee would.

scoring_methodology.name: Weighted geometric-mean desirability (multi-parameter optimization)
scoring_methodology.why_geometric_mean: Each endpoint is mapped to a desirability d in [0,1] (Harrington 1965; Derringer & Suich 1980) and aggregated as a WEIGHTED GEOMETRIC MEAN: D = exp( sum_i w_i * ln(d_i) / sum_i w_i ). The geometric mean is the industry-standard MPO scalarization (it underpins QED, Bickerton 2012, Nat. Chem. 4:90, and the CNS-MPO desirability approach, Wager 2010, ACS Chem. Neurosci. 1:435). Unlike an arithmetic mean, a single near-zero desirability (e.g. a strong DILI signal) drags the whole composite down — you cannot 'average away' a safety liability with good permeability. This matches how committees actually triage and removes the false-positive/false-negative failure mode of additive scoring.
scoring_methodology.desirability_transform: Higher-is-better endpoint scores (potency, ADME, developability) map linearly: d = score/100. Liability probabilities use a Wager-style piecewise-linear desirability with two inflection points (watch threshold t_w, hard threshold t_h): d = 1 for p <= t_w (ideal/flat region), d declines linearly from 1.0 to d_min across [t_w, t_h], and d = d_min for p >= t_h. This credits a compound that is safely below the monitoring threshold and penalizes proportionally as the liability probability climbs toward the veto line.
references: Harrington E.C. (1965) The desirability function. Industrial Quality Control 21:494.
Derringer G., Suich R. (1980) Simultaneous optimization of several response variables. J. Quality Technology 12:214.
Bickerton G.R. et al. (2012) Quantifying the chemical beauty of drugs (QED). Nature Chemistry 4:90.
Wager T.T. et al. (2010) Moving beyond rules: CNS multiparameter optimization (CNS MPO). ACS Chem. Neurosci. 1(6):435-449.

Waring M.J. et al. (2015) An analysis of the attrition of drug candidates from four major pharmaceutical companies. Nat. Rev. Drug Discov. 14:475 — safety and PK are the leading causes of attrition, justifying the safety-weighted profile below.

veto_methodology.rationale: Hard vetoes are NOT averaged into the composite — they are deterministic stage-gates grounded in regulatory guidance. A genotoxic or torsadogenic alert stops a program regardless of how good the rest of the profile is. This mirrors real practice and the relevant ICH guidance.

regulatory_basis.ames_mutagenicity: ICH M7(R2) — (Q)SAR prediction of bacterial mutagenicity (Ames / OECD 471) is the gold-standard DNA-reactivity gate; a positive structural/QSAR concern requires control or de-selection.
regulatory_basis.herg_cardiac: ICH S7B + ICH E14 — IKr (hERG) block is the principal in-vitro signal for delayed ventricular repolarization / QT prolongation / torsades de pointes.
regulatory_basis.genotoxicity_carcinogenicity: ICH S2(R1) genotoxicity battery and ICH S1 carcinogenicity — positive findings trigger carcinogenic-risk consideration.
regulatory_basis.structural_alerts: Deterministic reactive/genotoxic substructure scans (Brenk, BMS, NIH/PAINS) — chemical liabilities independent of any probabilistic model.
regulatory_basis.developability: Lipinski Rule-of-5 (Lipinski 2001, Adv. Drug Deliv. Rev. 46:3) — >=3 violations predict poor oral developability.

veto_methodology.calibration_note: The pre-fix scorecard used 5 independent literature-default ML hard-veto gates (hERG 0.80, DILI 0.80, Ames 0.75, ClinTox 0.80, Carcinogen 0.80). Given the per-endpoint false-positive rate of ADMET-AI / CardioTox / DILI-ML on FDA-approved drugs (~10-18% each; TDC leaderboard AUROCs hERG 0.856, Ames 0.871, DILI 0.925), the union FPR for at least one gate to trip on a real drug is 1 - prod(1 - FPR_i) ~ 55%. That is why every FDA drug used to come back NO-GO. Thresholds below are re-fitted so the union FPR on a held-out FDA-approved set (~152 DrugCentral 2024 approved, withdrawn excluded) is <= 5% while recall on a published-liability set (terfenadine, cisapride, cerivastatin, troglitazone, rofecoxib, etc.) stays >= 90%. Recipe: scripts/recalibrate-l1-thresholds.mjs. The LOOKUP-FIRST path (drug_lookup.py) covers ~150 well-known drugs by exact/Tanimoto match — they bypass these gates entirely and return measured values. These thresholds apply ONLY to novel chemistry.

_meta.calibration_set: DrugCentral 2024 approved set (n=152) + withdrawn-liability set (n=18); TDC ADMET leaderboard for model AUROC priors
_meta.applicability_domain_gating: When AD label is 'Out-of-domain' (NN-Tanimoto < 0.40 to training set), the corresponding ML hard-veto is downgraded to WATCH. Out-of-domain ML predictions are extrapolations and must not act as hard vetoes.

mpo_weights._doc: Intended (pre-renormalization) weights for the MPO geometric-mean composite, grouped by axis. Renormalized over whichever dimensions are computable for a given molecule (an endpoint that cannot be computed is dropped, never defaulted). Aggregate safety weight (~0.44) exceeds efficacy/ADME/developability individually, reflecting that safety + PK are the leading causes of clinical attrition (Waring 2015). Sums to 1.00 when every dimension is present.

desirability._doc: Liability-probability desirability transform inflection points. d=1.0 at or below t_w; linear decline to d_min at t_h; d=d_min above t_h. d_min kept > 0 so a single endpoint cannot zero the geometric mean before the rule-based veto (which is the correct mechanism for a hard stop) has fired.
